title: Venue Reader project TOML configuration
description: Schema after removing known foreign editor settings and rejecting global-only candidates with a warning. Each matching .venue-reader.toml is a layer, merged root-to-leaf. No format version or dictionary version field exists.

path.description: One QuickFIX XML file: conventional FIX4, FIX5 application with bundled FIXT, or combined FIXT with explicit applicationVersion.

name.description: Unique name within the applicable configuration chain; duplicate names are errors.

default.description: Use this binding as an exact identity default after layer precedence. All conflicting effective claims are disabled; named selections remain available.

transport.description: Bundled identifier or QuickFIX XML file supplying the transport role; registration names are not sources.

application.description: Bundled identifier or QuickFIX XML file supplying the application role; registration names are not sources.

applicationVersion.description: Canonical application release; required for combined FIXT sources. Must agree with application XML release metadata.

extensionPack.description: Exact application extension pack; absence differs from zero.

dictionaries.description: Bindings accumulate under unique names. A stronger source replaces claims for the same exact identity before conflict checks. File sources require global allowDictionaryPath; bundled sources do not.

messageSummary.description: Everything about the one-line message summary, including which LSP channels carry it.

channels.description: Document-overridable output channels, constrained by advertised client capabilities. Enabling both draws the summary twice.

rules.description: Built-in diagnostic rules. Unknown identifiers are non-fatal configuration errors and are ignored.

integrity.description: Check presence of BeginString(8), BodyLength(9), and CheckSum(10) on every parsed field sequence. With BeginString(8) and at least two fields, also check length and checksum values and offer their joint repair. Never guess or insert BeginString(8).

dictionaryVersion.description: Selected dictionary and resolved message version do not match; one finding per mismatching version in each diagnostic walk.

unknownMsgType.description: A MsgType(35) the line's dictionary does not list. Silent under a dictionary that lists no session message, whose table cannot be trusted to be complete. Only on a line whose dictionary was chosen, not fallen back to.

unknownTag.description: A tag the line's dictionary does not define, at every occurrence; says how standard FIX sees the tag as hover does. Only on a line whose dictionary was chosen, not fallen back to.

template.description: The message symbol's name. Same slots as messageSummary.template; fields, groups and instances are not templated.

dictionary.description: Select a bundled/global/project dictionary name, or an allowed path. Relative selector paths must start with ./, ../, or ~/; other relative strings are names. This does not restrict dictionaries[].path.

files.description: Optional anchored case-sensitive glob filters relative to this directory; * and ? do not cross /, ** does. Absolute and escaping patterns are errors.

defaultApplVerID.description: Canonical application release used when ApplVerID(1128) is absent. A selected complete pair supplies its identity first. No application default is built in.

format.description: How the label is written: literal text plus a nameless hole, {}. Each setting draws one thing, so the hole needs no name: for tagNames it is what the tag is called (its group path inside a group, unless groupPaths is off), for enumValues it is what the value means. An empty hole suppresses the whole label including its literals, which is why a tag the dictionary does not define is passed over; a format with no hole is therefore drawn on every field. Write a literal brace by doubling it; the hole may appear more than once and each repeats the same value. The label reaches the client verbatim, newlines included, and what it does with them is the client's.
